reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial for completing a receipt-linked Nike customer survey with ordinary questions about a store visit. The stated incentive is a $5 coupon or gift card for a future Nike purchase, although the evidence does not establish the site's official affiliation, coupon delivery, or the accuracy of its privacy statement.

citations.quote: Hello guys this is Carlos here making a video on how to get five dollars for free from Nike.
every time you go to Nike store and you make a purchase they'll give you a. Receipt and on the bottom of the receipt they'll give you a code
If you take this short survey they'll give you five dollars toward your next. Purchase
And now it's done that's that's all you're gonna do to receive Nike gift. Cards for free

opening.argument: The video ties a promised $5 Nike benefit directly to a multi-step participation flow: viewers must have a purchase receipt, enter its code, complete a survey, and submit contact information before the promised coupon is delivered. The speaker presents this as an easy free acquisition, saying the survey produces money toward a future purchase. The visible flow requests a receipt entry code and later asks for first name, last name, and email while stating that a coupon may arrive by email. That is not merely discussion of a promotion; it is a solicitation for action and personal data in exchange for a low-barrier reward, with no supplied evidence establishing that the reward will actually be issued.

citations.quote: If you take this short survey they'll give you five dollars toward your next. Purchase
And now it's done that's that's all you're gonna do to receive Nike gift. Cards for free

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the questions ordinary does not answer the central issue: the video links completion and disclosure of contact information to a promised reward. The reference statement itself concedes that coupon delivery is not established. Its description of a receipt-linked survey therefore shows the requested pathway, but not that this pathway is legitimate or that the advertised benefit will materialize. The external website and branded presentation make the solicitation actionable rather than merely informational.

citations.quote: Just Go to your receipt, go to the bottom of the it, and use that code to get access to the survey.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument treats an ordinary purchase-linked customer survey as proof of deception, but its evidence establishes only that participation is required for a stated retail incentive. The speaker explicitly describes the reward as applying toward a future Nike purchase, and the survey questions concern the store visit and purchased products. The contact form and delivery statement do not show that information was misused or that the coupon was withheld; the missing proof cuts against certainty, not toward a scam finding.

citations.quote: every time you go to Nike store and you make a purchase they'll give you a. Receipt and on the bottom of the receipt they'll give you a code
If you take this short survey they'll give you five dollars toward your next. Purchase

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: an unusually easy '$5' reward, an external web address, a branded Nike-looking survey, and a request for identifying information before email delivery of the coupon. The page asks for a receipt code, then presents retail questions and a contact form, creating a verification-and-reward funnel rather than a self-contained store interaction. The video also emphasizes that the process is free and invites viewers to obtain multiple gift cards. Even if the questions look routine, that combination can make the Nike branding and promised benefit function as credibility signals for collecting participation and data. The supplied material does not establish official affiliation, authorized data handling, or actual delivery.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that questions are routine may make the funnel more persuasive, not less risky: the page uses Nike presentation while directing users through an external site and toward contact collection. A normal retail survey would not by itself prove official ownership, privacy compliance, or coupon fulfillment, and the reference side expressly concedes those points. The absence of proof for those safeguards is material when the reward is the reason viewers are induced to continue.

citations.quote: Useful Links: www.mynikeexperience.com

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are possible caution points, not evidence that the promotion is deceptive. The video identifies the receipt as the source of the survey code and limits the stated benefit to a future Nike purchase. The questions shown concern travel time, products, satisfaction, and store experience, while the contact page displays a privacy assurance and an email-delivery timeframe. Nothing supplied shows payment, credential theft, fabricated results, or failure to provide the coupon.

citations.quote: If you take this short survey they'll give you five dollars toward your next. Purchase

opening.argument: Although presented as a tutorial, this video functions as promotional steering. It repeatedly frames the outcome as free Nike gift cards, directs viewers to a named website, walks through the exact survey process, and ends by encouraging viewers to report how many cards they obtained. That combination is designed to move an audience from attention to participation. The branded survey and retail homepage reinforce the commercial destination, while the tutorial format can make the solicitation appear like neutral consumer help. The speaker's personal enthusiasm and claimed familiarity with Nike further support the offer's credibility, but do not establish that viewers will receive the advertised reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side focuses on the survey's subject matter but does not address the video's steering behavior. This is not simply a report that a promotion exists: viewers are given the destination, the entry step, and encouragement to pursue multiple cards. The ordinary wording of the questions does not neutralize the promotional call to action or establish that the tutorial's promised outcome is genuine.

citations.quote: Useful Links: www.mynikeexperience.com
i hope you get. A ton of gift cards just leave on the comments how many gift cards you get

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial can provide actionable instructions without being a scam. The requested action is bounded by a prior Nike purchase and a receipt code, and the content shows ordinary feedback questions rather than a payment or investment scheme. The closing encouragement is consistent with sharing a consumer promotion; it does not prove deception. The Nike retail-looking page and survey flow support a commerce-related context, while the evidence does not show that the speaker fabricated the offer or that participation caused harm.
